blocks.content: The project portal dashboard is an overview of sales and projects: the numbers of sales leads, orders, projects and log entries, quick links, recent activity and the state of the public part of the portal.
The whole application works as a chain: sales lead → link to the order form → order → project → client portal, where the client follows the progress, communicates and approves.

sections.heading: 01. Header and state of the portal

blocks.content: The header Project portal overview shows the time of the last update and the Refresh button (it also reloads the state of the portal). On the right is the state of the public part: Online (green), Online · problem (orange - errors in the log in 24 hours or a slow response), Offline · maintenance (red) or Unavailable.

With the permission to switch the public portal and the order form off / on (project-portal-set-maintenance-mode) there is the button Switch application off / Switch application on next to it; confirm the change with your password (procedure in the chapter Applications).

Switched-off portal: the client portal of projects and the order form show the maintenance page (/projects/maintenance) and clients can neither sign in nor send an order. After switching on, a client returns to where they were by opening the maintenance page. The administration keeps running.

blocks.content: Each tile, card and the activity are shown only with the permission for their page. The main tile and the overviews work the same as on the system dashboard.

A sales lead is a potential client a salesperson is dealing with. For a lead you record the contact, the source channel, the state of the talks, the priority, contact dates and the next step. When the client decides to order, you send them a link to the order form - the submitted form creates an order and the order a project.

steps.label: Talks
steps.text: Record the status, the last contact and the next step.

steps.label: Link to the form
steps.text: The Link button creates a link to the order form for the client.

steps.label: Order
steps.text: The client fills in and sends the form; an order is created and the lead switches to the status Inquiry form sent.

steps.label: Project

blocks.content: Columns: ID, Subject / Company, Status, Priority, Salesperson, Last contact, Created. Filters by ID, company, status, priority and salesperson. The lead details show the contact person, e-mail, phone, other contact, location, source channel and source URL, the dates of the first and last contact, the next step, the note and the rejection reason.

cards.title: Subject / Company name
cards.text: Required, at least 2 characters.

cards.title: Contact person, Email, Phone
cards.text: Whom to address.

cards.title: Location
cards.text: City or region.

cards.title: Source channel
cards.text: Where the lead came from - LinkedIn, Facebook, Instagram, X, WhatsApp, Telegram, website form, e-mail, phone, in-person meeting, networking, referral, former client, inquiry portal, Google Business Profile, paid ad, partner, other online / offline channel.

cards.title: Current status
cards.text: New, In communication, Preparing offer, Offer sent, Inquiry form sent, Negotiating, On hold, Handed to dev team, Closed - Won, Awaiting invoicing, Awaiting payment, Paid - Project started, Closed - Lost, Other.

cards.title: Priority
cards.text: Low, Below average, Neutral, High, Critical.

cards.title: First contact / Last contacted
cards.text: Dates of the talks. By the date of the last contact the calendar reminds you of a lead nobody has talked to for 14 days or more.

cards.title: Next step
cards.text: What needs to be done next.

cards.title: Case note and Rejection reason
cards.text: Details; fill in the reason for a lost lead.

blocks.content: The salesperson of a new lead is automatically the person who created it.

steps.label: Link
steps.text: The Link button in the row of a lead creates the link and copies it to the clipboard (message “Link copied” with the validity date).

steps.label: Send it to the client
steps.text: Paste the link into your e-mail or message to the client.

steps.label: Form
steps.text: On the link the client sees the order form prefilled with the data of the lead. They add the name or company name, company ID, e-mail, phone, address, the order description, attachments and confirm the consent to the terms and conditions and to the processing of personal data.

items: The link is valid for 30 days; every new press of Link extends the validity by another 30 days from that moment.
Only one order can be sent from one lead - a used link tells the client they already sent the form.
An expired unused link is replaced by a new one on the next press of Link (the old one stops working).
The end of the link's validity is shown in the calendar (Form expires).
The link contains only a random code, never the internal number of the lead. Invalid attempts are written to the security monitoring.

blocks.content: Add leads from another register with Import data in the Actions menu (CSV or XLSX). Download the template, fill it in, have the file checked and confirm. The window shows the allowed values of statuses, priorities and sources. The procedure is in the introductory chapter.

Delete leads one by one or in bulk (checkboxes → Delete selected) to the trash; in the trash you restore them or delete them permanently. Old leads are deleted automatically by retention (Legal documents → Data retention, row Leads).
Leads contain personal data of contact persons. Protect exports and delete leads you no longer need.

Orders without a project yet are recalled by the calendar in the panel Waiting for you.

steps.label: Link from a lead
steps.text: The salesperson sends the client a link (page Sales leads, button Link).

steps.label: Form
steps.text: At the address /projects/order/<code> the client fills in the order in the language of the page and sends it. Older links /order_form/<code> still work.

steps.label: Saving
steps.text: An order is created with the salesperson of the lead; the lead is marked as sent.

steps.label: Confirmation
steps.text: The client receives a confirmation e-mail in the language of the form (chapter 04).

blocks.highlight: When the portal is switched off
blocks.content: In maintenance mode the form accepts no orders.

Columns: ID, Client, Salesperson, Company ID, Created; filters by ID, client, salesperson and company ID. The details show the e-mail, phone, address, the order description, the data processing consent (GDPR), the terms and conditions consent, attachments (View / Download) and the dates of creation and the last change.
The record of consents is evidence in case of a dispute - do not change it and keep orders with it for the period required by accounting and tax rules.

The Project button (folder icon) in a row opens the project of the order. When the order has none yet, the form of a new project opens with the order selected and the name and contact of the client prefilled. Creating a project and giving the client access to the portal are described in the chapter Projects.

In the Actions menu choose Edit confirmation e-mail. You edit the text the client receives after sending the form: subject, heading, greeting (the client's name is added), intro message, the heading and labels of the summary (name / company, company ID, e-mail, phone, address, description, attachments, date) and the closing message - separately for every language. An empty field uses the Czech text, or the default English wording - empty fields are therefore marked orange and every language shows their number. The live preview shows the e-mail with sample data.

items: Edit opens the form: Client name / Company (required), Company ID, Client e-mail, Phone, Client address, Order description (required) and Attachments / Contract - you can add more files (up to 10 files, 20 MB per file, 50 MB in total).
Delete moves an order to the trash (also in bulk); in the trash you restore it or delete it permanently.
The retention of orders is set in Legal documents → Data retention (row Orders) - accounting rules may require keeping them up to 10 years.

blocks.content: The project list shows all customer projects, their assignees and how many client messages wait to be read or answered. Every project has its own page split into sub-pages (Overview, Conversations, Progress, Approvals, Updates, Access, Files, Settings). The client sees the project in the client portal and signs in with a personal account - a password, or a one-time code or link from an e-mail.

cards.title: Open a project
cards.text: The folder icon of a row opens the project page on the Overview sub-page (address project-portal/projects/ID/overview). The pencil icon offers a quick edit in a dialog.

cards.title: Assignee
cards.text: The Assignee column shows the administrator responsible for the project. The My projects filter keeps only your projects. Only an active administrator who may edit projects can be the assignee.

cards.title: New messages and Waiting on us
cards.text: New messages = client messages nobody in the administration has read yet (filter Unread messages). Waiting on us = open threads where the client wrote last and waits for a reply.

cards.title: New project
cards.text: The form lets you pick a template - the project then gets its checkpoints with dates counted from today. After creating, the Access sub-page opens: the project has no user yet, and without one nobody can sign in to the portal.

cards.title: Project templates
cards.text: The Templates toolbar button opens the template management (project-portal/projects/templates). A template has a name, description and a list of checkpoints, each with a title, description and an optional due date as days from the start (0-3650). Rows are added, moved with arrows and removed. Deleting a template does not change projects made from it.

blocks.content: The header shows the name, status, visibility, assignee and the number of unread messages, with the sub-page tabs below. Every sub-page has its own address (e.g. project-portal/projects/7/conversations), so you can send it to a colleague or open it from an e-mail; switching tabs keeps unsaved settings. The Conversations tab shows the unread messages, the Approvals tab the requests waiting for the client.

cards.title: Overview
cards.text: Key numbers (waiting on us, approvals, progress, users, updates) - a click opens the sub-page - and what happened in the last 90 days: client messages, approval decisions, step changes, published updates. An item opens its place, a message the thread itself.

cards.title: Settings
cards.text: Name, assignee, lead, contacts, dates, visibility and status are edited in the form - a change shows the Save changes / Discard changes bar. Leaving with unsaved changes or an uncopied password asks first.

cards.title: Who gets team e-mails
cards.text: A client message goes to the thread assignee, otherwise the project assignee, otherwise the contact e-mail of the project. Client approval decisions are delivered the same way.

blocks.content: The Access sub-page holds the portal link (Copy link) and the list of client users. Every person on the client side has their own account: name (shown with their messages), login name (3-64 characters: lower-case letters, digits, dot, dash, underscore; unique in the project), an optional e-mail and the e-mail language (prefill only). The client cannot change the name, login name or password; in the portal they set only their e-mail and notifications.

steps.label: Add a user
steps.text: Fill in the name and login name and choose the access: with a password (typed in, at least 10 characters with letters and digits, or generated), send an invitation by e-mail, or both. An account without a password needs an e-mail and an invitation.

steps.label: Invitation
steps.text: An e-mail with a link that signs the client in with one click (valid 7 days, once). The envelope icon of an account sends it again any time - older links stop working.

steps.label: Handing over a password
steps.text: The password is shown only once. Copy sign-in details copies the link, login name and password at once. The password is never stored (only its hash).

steps.label: Forgotten password
steps.text: The client can sign in with a code from the e-mail. The key icon resets the password: a new one is generated, the old one stops working and the user is signed out everywhere.

steps.label: Removal
steps.text: The bin icon removes the user and signs them out. Their messages and decisions stay under their name.

cards.title: Sign-in with a code
cards.text: On the portal sign-in page the client picks Code by e-mail and enters the login name or e-mail. If the account has an e-mail, a six-digit code arrives (valid 15 minutes, 5 attempts, at most 5 codes an hour). The answer is always the same, so it does not reveal whether the account exists.

cards.title: Verified e-mail
cards.text: Using a code or a link verifies the e-mail of the account. When the e-mail changes, the verification is dropped and the notifications are switched off. An account shows the chips With password / No password, Invited and E-mail verified.

cards.title: E-mail notifications
cards.text: The client switches them on in the portal (My account), separately for: a reply in a thread, a step state change, a step date change, a new update and an approval request. Everything is off by default; the administration only shows the choice.

cards.title: What the e-mail contains
cards.text: Only the project name, the subject of the thread / step / update / request and a link to the portal - never the message text. The link opens the right part of the portal.

blocks.content: With the move to users, the former shared password of every project became a user with the login name klient (the password stayed the same). All existing sign-ins ended - the client signs in again with klient and their password. You can rename the user klient or create personal accounts instead.

Conversations show the threads of this project, split into Mine, Active, Closed and All. A thread with unread messages shows their number; opening it marks it read for the whole administration. An open thread shows Waiting on us or Waiting on the client and the thread assignee. The list refreshes itself every minute. An open thread adds its new messages every 15 s - from the client, replies of colleagues and their internal notes - and updates “read by the client”; new client messages are marked read by this. If you scrolled up in the messages, the position stays. A hidden browser tab checks nothing.

cards.title: Thread assignee
cards.text: In an open thread you pick the administrator responsible for it; they get an e-mail and from then on receive the client messages of the thread. The Mine filter shows the threads assigned to you.

cards.title: Reply to the client
cards.text: The message is signed with your name, the client sees it in the portal and users who switched on reply notifications get an e-mail.

cards.title: Internal note
cards.text: The Internal note switch above the message field: the note (with attachments) is seen only by the team, marked yellow, never shown to the client and does not change Waiting on us / on the client.

cards.title: Read by the client
cards.text: Your messages show Not read yet or Read by the client.

blocks.content: Checkpoints are the project steps the client sees in the portal under Progress. Each has a title, optional description, due date and an internal note the client never sees. The state is picked from a menu (Not started, In progress, Done); a state or date change e-mails the users who switched that on. Arrows change the order; an overdue step is marked.

cards.title: Apply a template
cards.text: Adds the checkpoints of a template after the existing ones; the dates are counted from the chosen start date.

cards.title: Save as a template
cards.text: Creates a new template from the checkpoints of the project (dates become days from the first date).

blocks.content: Use an approval request when you need a binding consent from the client - for a design, texts or the hand-over of a finished part. A request has a title, description, files, optionally a project step and the date by which the client should respond. Users with the notification switched on get an e-mail.

steps.label: Ask for approval
steps.text: The New request button. Until the client decides, the request can be changed (files too).

steps.label: The client decides
steps.text: In the portal they choose Approve, or Request changes with a required comment. The decision is saved with the account and time and cannot be changed; the assignee gets an e-mail.

steps.label: After changes
steps.text: For a request with Changes requested choose Ask again - the request goes back to the client, the history of decisions stays.

steps.label: Cancel and delete
steps.text: A cancelled request is hidden from the client. Only a request without a decision can be deleted; the others are a record.

blocks.content: Updates are news about the progress of the project (what is done, what is happening, what comes next), possibly with files. Write a draft and publish it later, or publish at once. The client sees only published updates; an e-mail is sent only at the first publication, not after an edit or publishing again. A published update can go back to a draft or be deleted.

The Files sub-page gathers the attachments of all threads, updates and approval requests, newest first, with size, date, author and a link to where they come from. Attachments of internal notes are marked Internal and hidden from the client, as are the files of draft updates and cancelled requests. Download links are time-limited.

sections.heading: 09. What the client sees in the portal

blocks.content: The client signs in through the project link - with a password, a code from the e-mail or the invitation link (a sign-in lasts 24 hours from the last activity). The portal looks like the administration: at the top left “Client: name of the signed-in account” and “Project: name”, refresh and language on the right; on the left a menu with counts (news, approvals, unread messages, progress), at the bottom My account, Help and Log out. Every part has its own address (…/projects/{token}/overview, /checkpoints, /threads, /approvals, /updates, /files, /contacts, /account, /help), so a reload keeps the client in place and a link of an e-mail opens the right part directly. The Help part is a detailed guide for non-technical users (first steps, signing in, every part of the menu, notifications, security) in Czech and English.

cards.title: Overview
cards.text: What is new since the last visit (new items highlighted), a notice of requests waiting for approval, progress in per cent, threads waiting for the client, the estimated date and the current step.

cards.title: Progress and Communication
cards.text: Checkpoints with dates and descriptions; threads with priority, Waiting on you / Supplier is replying and the authors of messages.

cards.title: Approvals and Updates
cards.text: Requests with description, files, step, deadline and the history of decisions, with Approve / Request changes; published updates with files.

cards.title: Files, Contacts, Help
cards.text: All public files with a link to their source, the project lead contact and the supplier's company details, the portal guide.

cards.title: My account
cards.text: Name and login name (read-only), the sign-in method and the e-mail verification, e-mail, e-mail language and five notification switches (all off by default, they cannot be switched on without an e-mail).

blocks.content: Without the project-portal-projects-update permission the project page and the template management are read-only. The audit log records changes of the project, users (by id only), invitations and sign-ins by code / link (without the code and e-mail), checkpoints, thread assignment, approval requests with decisions (without the comment) and updates (without the text); messages, codes and passwords are never logged. Unused and expired sign-in codes are deleted automatically.

The sign-in of a client is held by the server only: after a successful sign-in the API sets a cookie (HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Strict) valid only for the addresses of that project. The JavaScript of the portal cannot see it and nothing is stored in localStorage, so a script cannot steal it. The session ends after 24 hours of inactivity, with a logout (deleted on the server), a password reset or when the user is removed. The API checks it on every request; as soon as it answers 401 the portal sends the client to the sign-in page of the project.

steps.label: Project link
steps.text: The client opens /projects/{token}. Before the portal shows, the application asks the API whether there is a valid session.

steps.label: No session
steps.text: Redirect to /projects/login/{token}. The section the client wanted (e.g. Approvals from an e-mail) and a one-time ?access= link are kept.

steps.label: Sign-in
steps.text: With a password, a code from the e-mail (15 minutes, 5 tries) or the link of an invitation / e-mail (one-time). The server sets the cookie and the portal opens the requested section.

steps.label: Working in the portal
steps.text: The thread list (badges) refreshes every 15 s, so does an open thread. A failed refresh is just skipped; a 401 ends the work and opens the sign-in.

steps.label: Logout
steps.text: Log out ends the session on the server; the same cookie is no longer valid anywhere.

cards.title: One-time link
cards.text: The link of an invitation (7 days) and of a sign-in e-mail (15 minutes) works only once; the database holds only its fingerprint (SHA-256), a new link cancels older unused ones. Opening a used link again does not sign in - but if the browser still has a valid session, the portal simply opens (the session signed in, not the link). In another browser or a private window the sign-in page appears.

cards.title: One account per browser
cards.text: A browser holds only one session per project. When another user of the same project signs in in it (e.g. with the link of their e-mail), the cookie is replaced. Open tabs notice it when the window is used again: they ask the API who is signed in and switch to the new account (header, sides of the messages, My account). So the portal never shows another account than the one the API saves the messages for. Two users at once = two browsers or a private window.

cards.title: Portal maintenance
cards.text: A switched-off portal (settings of the application) answers 503 and the client sees the Maintenance page with the text of the settings; once it is on again, opening (or reloading) the page returns them where they were.

cards.title: Separated from the administration
cards.text: The requests of the portal go without the sign-in of the administration and the portal never gets internal data: internal notes, internal notes of steps, draft updates, cancelled requests or internal attachments are not sent to the client at all.

sections.heading: 11. Common situations and how to solve them

cards.title: The client cannot sign in
cards.text: Check the login name and the labels of the account on the Access subpage. A forgotten password: the client can sign in with a code by e-mail (the account needs an e-mail), or reset the password with the key icon and hand over the new one. The portal must not be switched off (maintenance) and the project must be visible.

cards.title: The invitation link does not work
cards.text: It was used already, expired (7 days) or you sent a newer invitation meanwhile. Send the invitation again with the envelope icon, or let the client sign in with a code by e-mail.

cards.title: The code did not arrive
cards.text: The account has no e-mail, the e-mail ended in spam, or the client used up 5 codes an hour. For security the form always answers the same, so the client does not see the reason - check the e-mail of the account and the audit log.

cards.title: Messages show under another name
cards.text: Two users of the same project in one browser: whoever signed in last counts and the open tabs switch to them. Advise the client to use a separate browser or a private window for each person.

cards.title: The client gets no notifications
cards.text: The client turns them on in My account and they need an e-mail; everything is off by default. Changing the e-mail turns the notifications off and removes the confirmation.

cards.title: A file does not download
cards.text: Download links expire after a while. The client opens Files again or clicks refresh at the top right - new links load.

blocks.content: The project portal log is the history of all actions in the application: in the administration (leads, orders, projects, milestones, templates, client accounts, approvals, updates, threads, settings, maintenance) and the activity of clients in the portal (sign-ins, new threads, approval decisions, attachment downloads).
Entries cannot be edited or deleted. The log does not contain the texts of clients' messages.

sections.heading: 01. What you find in the log

cards.title: Administration
cards.text: Creations, edits, deletions and restorations; status and order of milestones; new, edited, applied and deleted templates; new, edited and deleted client accounts, new password and invitation; approval requests (new, edit, reopening, cancelation, deletion); updates; assigning, closing and reopening a thread; generating a lead link; imports, exports and reports.

cards.title: Client portal
cards.text: Sign-in and logout of a client, a sent sign-in code, account settings by the client, a new thread and a change of its status, an approval decision, an attachment download.

cards.title: Operation
cards.text: Change of the maintenance mode, an unauthorized maintenance toggle attempt, errors.

cards.title: Modules
cards.text: Projects, Milestones, Project templates, Client accounts, Approvals, Updates, Communication, Client portal, Sales leads, Orders, Portal settings.

blocks.content: Filter entries by user, event, module and IP address, open the details with technical data, export them and draw charts - the same as in System logs.
When did the client last sign in? - event Client signed in. Who approved a change? - Client approval decision. Who sent the client an invitation? - Client invited.
The log contains e-mails and IP addresses - protect exports and delete them after use.
The permission to show the log history of the project portal (project-portal-view-logs).
